sections.heading: How to automate a stock strategy from TradingView

body.html: Automating a stock strategy takes four steps and no programming:

items: Connect your broker. Create a PickMyTrade account and connect your Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, or Tradier account. You can use a live account or a paper / demo account where your broker offers one.
Generate your alert. In PickMyTrade, generate the alert message and the webhook URL for your buy and sell signals. PickMyTrade writes this for you, so there is no JSON to hand-code.

Paste it into TradingView. Create an alert on your strategy or indicator in TradingView, delete the default message, paste the PickMyTrade message, and set the webhook URL in the alert's Notifications tab. Webhook alerts require a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+, or Premium), because free TradingView accounts cannot send webhooks.

Go live. Enable the alert. When it fires, PickMyTrade places the stock order at your broker automatically. Test on a small size first, then confirm the fill in your PickMyTrade alert log and in your brokerage account.

sections.heading: The pattern day trader (PDT) rule and day-trading considerations

body.html: Automating stock trades does not exempt you from US day-trading rules, so it is worth understanding the pattern day trader (PDT) rule before you switch a strategy on. Under long-standing FINRA rules, if you place four or more day trades within five business days in a margin account, and those trades make up more than 6% of your total trades in that period, you are flagged as a pattern day trader and must keep at least $25,000 in equity in that account. Fall below $25,000 and your broker can restrict day trading until you top the account back up.
A few practical points for automated stock strategies:

items: The rule applies to margin accounts. Cash accounts are not subject to the PDT count, but they settle on a delay, so you can only trade with settled funds, which limits how often you can round-trip the same money.
The rule is about intraday round trips. Strategies that hold overnight are generally not counted as day trades.
Futures are not subject to the PDT rule, which is one reason some automated traders run intraday strategies on futures instead of stocks.

body.html: Rules like these change over time, and your broker may apply them slightly differently, so confirm the current requirements with your broker before you automate an intraday stock strategy. For a fuller walkthrough, read our guide on day trading rules and PDT requirements.
PickMyTrade places real broker orders, not just notifications, so you get proper order control on every automated stock trade:

items: Order types: Market, Limit, and Stop orders.
Stop-loss and take-profit: attach protective exits to each entry so a position is managed even when you are away from the screen.
Position sizing: size each trade by a fixed number of shares or by a risk percentage of the account.
Multi-account: send one alert to more than one connected account at the same time, each with its own sizing.

body.html: Everything runs in the cloud, so there is no desktop app to keep open and no VPS to rent. You set the rules once, and PickMyTrade applies them to every alert.

sections.heading: How to automate an options strategy from TradingView

body.html: The flow is the same whether you trade one contract or a four-leg spread: an alert leaves TradingView, PickMyTrade receives it, and the order lands at your broker. Here is the full alert-to-execution path.

items: Connect your options broker. Create a PickMyTrade account and connect your Interactive Brokers or Tradier account. This is where your options orders will be placed, so use a paper or simulated account first while you test.

Set your rules in PickMyTrade. Choose how each alert should behave: the option type, how strikes and expiries are chosen, position size (a fixed number of contracts or a risk-percentage of the account), and any stop-loss or take-profit. PickMyTrade can select strikes based on real-time prices and the rules you define, so you are not hard-coding a single strike into every alert.

Generate the webhook and paste it into TradingView. PickMyTrade gives you an alert message and a webhook URL. In TradingView, create an alert on your strategy or indicator, delete the default message, paste the PickMyTrade message, and set the webhook URL in the alert's notifications tab. Webhook alerts need a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+, or Premium), since free TradingView accounts cannot send webhooks. There is nothing to code.

Test, then go live. Fire a test alert, confirm the order in your PickMyTrade log and in your broker, then enable the alert. From that point your strategy runs on its own. On speed: PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side. Total fill time also depends on your broker's execution, network latency, and how quickly TradingView sends the alert.

body.html: Multi-leg options automation is where a rules-based tool earns its keep. Placing a four-leg iron condor by hand means legging into a short call spread and a short put spread while prices move against you. An automated iron condor system sends all of that from one TradingView alert, so the legs go out together instead of one click at a time.

With PickMyTrade you can automate the strategies most range-bound and premium-selling traders use: verticals, butterflies, and full iron condors. Because you define the legs, strikes, and widths in your rules, an automated iron condor on SPX or another underlying follows the exact structure you designed, every time the alert fires. This is genuine multi-leg options automation, not a black box: you decide the strategy and PickMyTrade executes it.

For a step-by-step walkthrough of building an automated iron condor, including how the four legs map to your alert, read our full guide: Automate Iron Condor: multi-leg options automation guide. If you trade options on Interactive Brokers specifically, our guide to automating options trading on Interactive Brokers covers the IB setup in detail.

sections.heading: Risk and order controls for options automation

body.html: An automated options trading bot is only as safe as the controls around it, so PickMyTrade puts risk settings on every alert rather than leaving them to chance.

items: Position sizing. Trade a fixed number of contracts per alert, or size the position so the maximum loss is a set percentage of the account. That keeps a single trade from oversizing the account.
Stop-loss and take-profit. Attach exits to the order so the strategy manages itself instead of relying on you to watch the screen.
Strike and expiry rules. Define how strikes and expiries are chosen so the same logic applies whether the alert fires today or next week.

You stay in control. PickMyTrade does not provide trading signals or investment advice. It executes your rules. Automated systems act on predefined logic and may not adapt to sudden market moves, and options trading carries real risk, including losing 100% of the premium paid. Test in paper trading first.
